page: The Vultr vx1-m-16c-128gb is a memory-optimized cloud instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC processor cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates advanced instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is limited to a 1 GB local NVMe SSD boot disk, and one public IPv4 address is provided with no hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance alongside balanced multi-core throughput. In synthetic processor benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution (3618.18) and high text-processing throughput in Geekbench (3068.0). Decompression workloads perform particularly well, with single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching top-tier throughput of 17.64 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression recording 39.73 GB/sec. Large uncached memory bandwidth sustains 88.71 GB/sec for reads and 45.71 GB/sec for writes. PassMark tests evaluate the memory subsystem at a strong 2871.66, while multi-core compute tests place the system solidly within average tiers.

From an operational and cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high memory density relative to core count without requiring oversized compute allocations. A notable design tradeoff is the minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD, which is sufficient only for initial boot and basic system overhead. Applications requiring persistent local storage will require detached block storage solutions. The provision of dedicated physical cores ensures predictable, non-burstable execution without neighbor interference.

Given its heavy memory weighting and vector instruction support, the Vultr vx1-m-16c-128gb is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, medium-scale data science preprocessing, and high-concurrency memory-resident microservices.
description: The Vultr vx1-m-16c-128gb is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance designed for memory-intensive workloads. It is powered by 16 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, supporting AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The server includes 128 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration. Local storage is constrained to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, making external block storage necessary for persistent operational data. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compression and execution performance, supported by strong memory metrics in PassMark and consistent Redis throughput. Due to its high memory density and dedicated core allocation, this instance fits in-memory caching layers, Redis instances, extract-transform-load (ETL) processing pipelines, and memory-resident analytical databases.
